summary:
KOZ Atlas is an end-to-end scientific harmonization and decision-support platform that unifies 20+ years of NASA MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active fire and thermal anomaly records into a single, consistent Burning Activity Calendar. Directly combining raw MODIS and VIIRS observations creates artificial post-2012 fire frequency jumps (~3.8x) because a single 1 km MODIS fire footprint fractures into 4–12 VIIRS sub-pixels (~7.1x areal difference), while VIIRS also captures low-intensity fires (<12 MW) below the MODIS threshold. Furthermore, following the November 2, 2026 retirement of the Suomi-NPP VIIRS NRT stream and the upcoming 2027 decommissioning of Terra/Aqua MODIS, seamless cross-sensor continuity with NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 is critical.

KOZ Atlas resolves this through a 4-stage Zero-Data-Leakage pipeline: (1) Schema standardization and confidence alignment across MODIS and VIIRS archives/live feeds, (2) Orbit-aware 4D KD-tree and spherical Haversine clustering (Δd ≤ 1.2 km, |Δt| ≤ 60 min) that merges redundant sub-pixels into unified fire events, (3) Time-block Huber log1p(FRP) radiometric calibration and empirical detectability weighting to align VIIRS energy onto the historical MODIS baseline, and (4) 0.01° (~1 km) spatial persistence filtering to isolate static industrial flares and refineries (Type=2) from true ecological wildfires.
details:
### Overview & Core Architecture

KOZ Atlas (Live Web App: https://kozatlas-main.streamlit.app/ | GitHub Repository: https://github.com/MehmetHalilKILIC/kozatlas | 7-Slide Deck: https://github.com/MehmetHalilKILIC/kozatlas/tree/main/presentation) transforms fragmented multi-satellite hotspot feeds into a calibrated, long-term wildfire intelligence system via a four-stage scientific pipeline:

1. Stage 1 — Multi-Sensor Ingestion & Schema Standardization:

Ingests NASA FIRMS Area API streams (automatically chunked into safe day-ranges) and historical Standard Product (SP) CSV archives across MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20/21). Standardizes brightness temperatures (brightness/bright_t31 and bright_ti4/bright_ti5), UTC timestamps, and unifies MODIS numeric (0–100) and VIIRS categorical (l/n/h) confidence levels onto a common scale.

2. Stage 2 — Orbit-Aware Spatiotemporal Haversine Clustering:

Uses a 4D KD-tree on the unit sphere combined with exact spherical Haversine distance (R = 6371.0 km) and temporal windows (default Δd ≤ 1.2 km, |Δt| ≤ 60 min) to cluster coincident sub-pixels into unified fire events (KOZ-YYYYMMDD-seq). Computes FRP-weighted centroids and classifies events as BOTH (MODIS+VIIRS), VIIRS_CLUSTER_HARMONIZED, or MODIS_ONLY.

3. Stage 3 — Time-Block Log-FRP Calibration & Detectability Weighting:

Trains a robust Huber regression model in log(1 + FRP) space on coincident MODIS+VIIRS events to calibrate VIIRS radiative power onto the MODIS scale. Evaluates empirical MODIS capture rates across six VIIRS FRP bins (0–5 MW to 80+ MW) and aggregates activity into 1 km Active Fire Cell-Days, reducing the post-2012 artificial sensor jump from ~3.8x down to ~1.1x.

4. Stage 4 — Static Industrial Source (Type=2) Isolation:

Identifies persistent ~1 km thermal cells active across ≥ 5 distinct days and ≥ 4 distinct months within a calendar year (gas flares, refineries, cement kilns) as Static Industrial Sites (STK-###), keeping the Burning Activity Calendar free of industrial false positives.

### Interactive Web Platform (4 Modules)

- Tab 1 (Interactive GIS Satellite Map): Canvas-accelerated Leaflet/Folium map with Esri Dark Canvas and Satellite Imagery basemaps displaying Raw MODIS (1 km), Raw VIIRS (375 m), KOZ Harmonized Events, and Static Industrial Sources.

- Tab 2 (Burning Activity Calendar): Year × Month heat matrix benchmarking any selected month against the 20+ year historical median with anomaly ratios (e.g., 1.00x = normal) and seasonal Q1–Q3 bands.

- Tab 3 (Sensor Harmonization Evidence): Pre/post-2012 jump metrics, log-FRP calibration scatter plots, and empirical MODIS detectability curves.

- Tab 4 (Data Download Center): One-click export of harmonized event catalogs (CSV), static industrial registries, and JSON provenance metadata.

### Benefits & Intended Impact

- Preserves 20+ Year Climate Continuity: Enables climate scientists, forestry agencies, and disaster response teams to compare current wildfire seasons (2024–2026+) directly against the 2000–2025 historical baseline without artificial sensor-transition bias.

- Ready for the Post-November 2026 Satellite Era: Seamlessly bridges the November 2, 2026 Suomi-NPP NRT retirement and the upcoming 2027 Terra/Aqua MODIS decommissioning by calibrating VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) onto a unified scale.

- Eliminates Industrial False Alarms: Automatically isolates persistent industrial heat sources (refineries, gas flaring stacks in basins like Batman/Southeastern Anatolia) from dynamic wildfires.

### Tools, Coding Languages & Creativity

- Stack: Python 3.11+, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy (4D cKDTree & Huber log-FRP regression), Streamlit, Folium/Leaflet HTML5 Canvas, and Plotly.

- Scientific Integrity: Enforces Zero Data Leakage and 5 scientific boundaries (no fake 375 m downscaling from 1 km MODIS, strict NRT vs. SP separation, and empirical detectability bounds).

- SI / AI Disclosure: SI tools assisted with code optimization, English translation, and presentation illustrations; all mathematical harmonization formulas were engineered and verified via deterministic unit tests.
